We test our homeowner tools where it matters most to us: at home.

The yard had a compacted, uneven surface, patchy drainage, an irregular shape that made the area easy to misjudge, and a 1 m drop along the left fence line, where the fence and part of the yard were slowly slumping into the neighbour's property.

We turned the lawn edges and bare ground into gravel paths, raised beds and drip irrigation, working out every quantity of soil, mulch and gravel first with the same free calculators on our [Homeowners page](../homeowners.qmd).  

![Before and after: bare ground and lawn edges turned into gravel beds and a raised garden bed.](../images/yard-before-after.jpg){fig-alt="Two photos side by side of the same backyard with a blue shed: before, with bare ground and a rough bed by the fence; after, with neat gravel borders, a raised bed and a hose."}

![The legal boss and professional hole digger checks the new raised bed. The wet circles show where each drip emitter waters the soil.](../images/raised-bed-drip-card.jpg){fig-alt="A husky sniffing a raised garden bed of dark soil with drip irrigation emitters, each surrounded by a circle of wet soil."}
